events.title: The election of Pope Benedict XVI
events.shortBlurb: The conclave chose the theologian Joseph Ratzinger to succeed John Paul II…
body: On 19 April 2005, on the fourth ballot of a two-day conclave, 115 cardinal electors chose Joseph Ratzinger, the 78-year-old German dean of the College of Cardinals, as the 265th bishop of Rome. From the loggia of St. Peter's he greeted the crowd as 'a simple, humble laborer in the vineyard of the Lord.'

Born at Marktl am Inn in Bavaria on 16 April 1927 and ordained priest in 1951, he had been a peritus at the Second Vatican Council, archbishop of Munich and Freising from 1977, and from 1981 prefect of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, the closest theological collaborator of John Paul II.

His pontificate gave the Church the encyclicals Deus Caritas Est, Spe Salvi, and Caritas in Veritate and the motu proprio Summorum Pontificum on the older liturgy. Citing failing strength of body and mind, he laid down the office on 28 February 2013, the first pope to do so since Gregory XII in 1415, and died at the Mater Ecclesiae monastery on 31 December 2022.
